sentences.text: Oweniasuchus is a member of the class Reptilia.
It belongs to the family Goniopholididae, a group of large marine reptiles.
The type species, O. major, comes from the Early Cretaceous Upper Purbeck Group in Beccles, England.
Originally, the species was known only from a mandibular ramus described by Richard Owen in 1879.
However, O. major is now considered a nomen dubium because its holotype specimen is too fragmentary for an adequate diagnosis.
Other species, O. lusitanicus and O. pulchelus, are known from the Late Cretaceous of Portugal.
The genus includes the type species O. major, as well as O. minor, O. lusitanicus, and O. pulchelus.
O. minor has been proposed as a synonym of the atoposaurid Theriosuchus pusillus.
Fossils of this animal date from the Berriasian to the Cenomanian stages, spanning the Early to Late Cretaceous periods.
Remains have been found in England and Portugal.
